**Reading time:** about 5 minutes. **Goal:** locate major events in time while recognizing where dates and biographical reports remain uncertain.

Plato lived through the last decades of the fifth century and much of the fourth century BC. The timeline begins with the war and epidemic that affected Athens **before** his probable birth. It then follows his association with Socrates, the founding of the Academy, his Sicilian connections and his death.

**How to read the dates:** An event stated simply as a year usually refers to a relatively well-established historical occurrence. “Around,” a range of years, or “according to tradition” signals a reconstruction or an ancient report of uncertain precision. Ages are deliberately omitted where dates are not secure.

The dates assigned to the **early, middle and late groups of dialogues** are not known with the precision of an annual history. The entries for these groups therefore describe a **relative literary chronology**, not specific years of publication.
